posts.cooked:
Hah, that’s not impossible. It depends on how the heroes shake out.

The big sticking point right now is the Southwest Sentinels and the Void Guard; if they stick with those decks, we need an expansion with the Sentinels, and we need an expansion that’s mostly Void Guard. The original Oblivaeon expansion had a ton of extra mini-expansion heroes released alongside it, which presumably isn’t going to be a thing this time.

So the question becomes - do all the ex-villains end up in Oblivaeon, and the Void Guard become the backbone of an expansion, or do Luminary and the Void Guard end up in Oblivaeon and we get our other ex-villains elsewhere?

I think the next two expansions are Vengeance/team Villains, and then Space (unsure on names).

Vengeance:

  1. Naturalist
  2. Akash’Thriya (those two should be together)
  3. Scholar
  4. Guise (again, should be together)
  5. SWS (don’t make sense in space, and take place in some team villain stuff afaik)
  6. Young Legacy

Space:
1-4. Void Guard (literally a space team)
5. Sky-Scraper (alien)
6. Fashion (space hero)

OA:

  1. Stuntman (reformed right before)
  2. Lifeline (reformed right before/hates OA)
  3. Luminary (reformed for OA)
  4. Comodora (does stuff to fight OA)
  5. Benchmark (late hero, no where else to go)
  6. Rambler (Grimm nemesis, sketchy character)

Those lineups just fit too neatly for me to not think that’ll be what happens.

Edit: Benchmark and Young Legacy could be swapped!

Why are Soul and Æterna so much more special from than other keywords?

Playtesters insisted on it, to the extent that we color-code our black-and-white prototypes every time Braithwhite hands us a new version. It’s vital that you be able to tell Soul from Æterna cards in your hand at a glance, especially if you build up a big hand.
